comparison: Perfect agreement on phylogenomic claims C2, C13, C23-C37. Both evaluations find the comprehensive presence/absence analysis of RIP kinases and RHIM proteins well-supported. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED with no concerns raised about the bioinformatic methodology or findings.

Both address RIPK1 RHIM dependence claims C54-C57. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED based on functional data. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 1's concern that experiments in human HEK293 cells may not reflect native function for evolutionarily distant species like lamprey and mussel.

Perfect claim overlap on ZBP1 and TRIF findings C58-C61. Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note these mechanistic findings about domain requirements are less subject to species-specific interpretation issues despite general concerns about heterologous expression.

Both address feline RIPK3 and NF-κB activation claims C4, C38-C40, C42-C43, C45. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 noting that while the general role is established, experimental restriction to human HEK293 cells means functionality of distant organisms' proteins may not reflect native context.

Both address RHIM tetrad conservation claims C5, C46-C49. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on positive selection analysis and sequence data. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, with editor noting 'compelling evidence' and reviewers not challenging the conservation findings despite rapid evolution in surrounding regions.

Both address positive selection in RIPK genes, with overlap on C20-C22. OpenEval covers broader set C18-C22 and finds SUPPORTED. Peer review addresses C3, C20-C22 and also finds SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 explicitly mentioning positive selection signals as part of the findings.

Both address RHIM variant functional tuning claims C6, C62-C64. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on systematic testing of natural variants. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN due to concerns that effects observed in human cells may not reflect native biology, particularly for distant species.

Both address positive selection in RIPK genes (C3). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on Figure 1B and supplementary files showing lineage-specific patterns. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 explicitly noting positive selection signals in certain mammalian clades.

Partial overlap on RHIM functional claims C50-C53. OpenEval R4 addresses tetrad conservation and finds SUPPORTED. Peer R6 addresses these claims along with C6, C62-C64 on functional tuning, rating as UNCERTAIN due to heterologous expression concerns for distant species.

Partial overlap on C18-C19 regarding RIPK4 and RIPK5 characterization. OpenEval R1 groups these with other positive selection findings and rates SUPPORTED. Peer R9 addresses these specifically as straightforward functional characterizations in native human system, also rated SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on cell death claims C41, C44. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on experimental data. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, applying the same heterologous expression caveat - functional assays in human cells may not reflect native context for distant organisms.

Both address tetrapod-specific emergence of CASP8 and ZBP1 (C67). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on phylogenomic evidence in Figure 1C. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, noting the phylogenetic distribution supports this inference though not explicitly commented on.

Minimal overlap on C7 regarding ancestral NF-κB function. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on collective data. Peer R3 addresses C7 along with other functional claims, rating as UNCERTAIN due to heterologous expression concerns.

Minimal overlap on C33 regarding RIPK2B in monotremes. OpenEval finds phylogenomic claim SUPPORTED as part of comprehensive analysis. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting this as an important finding not pursued experimentally, creating uncertainty about functional significance.

OpenEval R9 addresses background claims C1, C8-C17 establishing context from prior literature, rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.
OpenEval R10 addresses background claims C68-C76 from prior literature providing interpretive context, rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
